questions.questionText: Compare Malthusian and Boserupian theories regarding the relationship between population growth and food supply, evaluating which better explains modern agricultural trends in sub-Saharan Africa. [25 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [25 marks]
- **Malthus (1798):** Geometric population growth outstrips arithmetic food growth, triggering preventive (moral restraint) and positive checks (famine, war, disease) [8 marks].
- **Boserup (1965):** Rising population density acts as catalyst driving agricultural intensification (shortened fallow, irrigation, green-revolution hybrids, mechanisation) [9 marks].
- **Evaluation:** Boserup explains global yield surges where capital/extension exist, but localized Malthusian vulnerability persists under climate droughts, soil exhaustion, and weak rural infrastructure [8 marks].

questions.questionText: Analyse the five-stage Demographic Transition Model (DTM) and evaluate its applicability to the changing birth rates, death rates, and age pyramids of Zimbabwe and SADC nations. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **DTM Stages 1–5:** High stationary → Early expanding → Late expanding → Low stationary → Declining [8 marks].
- **Zimbabwe Application & Critique:** Zimbabwe reflects late Stage 2 / Stage 3 with falling fertility via female education and contraception alongside death rate fluctuations from HIV/AIDS impacts (now stabilising via ART), showing the Western Eurocentric model needs adaptation for health shocks and migration [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain Von Thünen's Agricultural Location Model, stating its simplifying assumptions and assessing why modern refrigeration, highways, and command policies distort its concentric land-use zones around Harare. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Model & Bid Rent:** Locational rent R = Y(P−C) − Y·t·d places perishable/high-transport-cost horticulture & dairying closest to the central market, then forestry, arable grains, and extensive ranching furthest out [10 marks].
- **Real-world Distortions:** Refrigerated trucks, multiple urban markets, fertile soil anisotropy, irrigation dams, and government pricing/land tenure distort ideal rings [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Evaluate Alfred Weber's Least-Cost Industrial Location Theory, distinguishing between weight-losing and weight-gaining industries with Zimbabwean manufacturing examples. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Weber Model:** Minimises transport cost (Locational Triangle of Material Index MI), labour cost, and agglomeration economies [8 marks].
- **Examples:** Weight-losing (MI > 1: iron smelting at Redcliff/Kwekwe, sugar milling in Lowveld, cement near limestone) locates at raw materials; Weight-gaining (MI < 1: soft-drink bottling, bakeries) locates at urban markets; evaluate neglect of tariffs, electricity availability, and environmental zoning [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Using Christaller's Central Place Theory (Threshold Population and Range of a Good), explain the hierarchy of urban settlements in Zimbabwe from rural growth points to Harare. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Concepts:** Range = max distance consumers travel; Threshold = min population/demand needed to sustain a service; Hexagonal non-overlapping service hinterlands (k=3,4,7) [9 marks].
- **Hierarchy:** Low-order rural service centres (groceries, primary clinic — small range/threshold) → District growth points/towns (bank, secondary hospital) → Bulawayo/Harare high-order regional cities (universities, specialist surgery, airports) [11 marks].

questions.questionText: Compare the concentric zone (Burgess), sector (Hoyt), and multiple-nuclei (Harris & Ullman) urban land-use models and evaluate how colonial planning shaped Harare's dual urban morphology. [25 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [25 marks]
- **Classic Models:** Burgess rings, Hoyt transport wedges, Harris & Ullman polycentric hubs [10 marks].
- **Harare Morphology:** Historical segregation placed low-density affluent suburbs (Borrowdale/Mount Pleasant) in well-drained northern sectors and high-density industrial-worker townships (Mbare, Highfield, Chitungwiza satellite) in southern/south-western sectors alongside industrial rail corridors—now modified by CBD edge office parks and peri-urban growth [15 marks].

questions.questionText: Assess the causes, socioeconomic contributions, and environmental/planning challenges of the Informal Sector in African cities. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Drivers:** Formal job contraction, rapid urban migration, low entry capital barriers [5 marks].
- **Contributions vs Challenges:** Provides livelihoods, cheap urban goods/recycling, and entrepreneurial incubators (Siya So / Magaba), yet creates congestion, unserviced sanitation waste, tax base erosion, and precarious worker safety [15 marks].

questions.questionText: With reference to Lee's Push-Pull Migration Model and Ravenstein's Laws, analyse the impacts of skilled international emigration ("brain drain") on Zimbabwe versus the role of diaspora remittances. [25 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [25 marks]
- **Push/Pull/Intervening Obstacles:** Economic opportunities & wage differentials pull nurses, engineers, and teachers abroad despite visa costs [8 marks].
- **Impacts:** Loss of public-funded human capital and strained clinics/schools vs substantial forex remittances sustaining household consumption, housing, and education fees [17 marks].

questions.questionText: Evaluate the causes and possible remedies for Urban Traffic Congestion in major cities such as Harare and Bulawayo. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Causes:** Dominance of private vehicles & low-capacity kombis, radial CBD concentration, uncoordinated traffic signals, absence of suburban light rail, peak commuter waves from Chitungwiza/Norton [8 marks].
- **Solutions:** High-capacity Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) / commuter rail corridors, park-and-ride hubs, outer ring-roads, decongesting offices to suburban nodes, congestion charging—evaluate funding & enforcement hurdles [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the "Resource Curse" hypothesis and assess how Mineral Beneficiation and Value Addition policies can transform Zimbabwe's mining sector (platinum, lithium, gold). [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Resource Curse:** Over-reliance on raw ore exports fuels price vulnerability, Dutch disease, weak linkages, and rent-seeking [7 marks].
- **Beneficiation:** Refining concentrates, manufacturing battery-grade lithium salts or platinum catalysts captures higher export value, builds engineering skills, and creates multiplier factories—constrained by reliable high-voltage power supply and refining capex [13 marks].

questions.questionText: Compare Rostow's Five Stages of Economic Growth with Friedmann's Core-Periphery Model in explaining regional development disparities within Zimbabwe. [25 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [25 marks]
- **Rostow:** Linear domestic stages (Traditional → Preconditions → Take-off → Maturity → Mass Consumption) criticised for ignoring colonial trade structures and external debt [10 marks].
- **Friedmann Core-Periphery:** Cumulative causation concentrates industry, talent, and investment in core hubs (Harare-Bulawayo rail spine) leaving peripheral rural districts lagging via backwash effects unless deliberate spread/decentralisation growth points intervene [15 marks].

questions.questionText: Evaluate the environmental, economic, and social impacts of Large-Scale Hydroelectric Dams (e.g., Kariba Dam) versus Distributed Solar Mini-Grids for rural energy security. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Large Hydro:** High baseload capacity and multi-purpose irrigation/fisheries, yet suffers severe El Niño drought vulnerability, community displacement, and huge grid transmission losses to remote villages [10 marks].
- **Solar Mini-Grids:** Fast modular deployment, zero transmission loss, climate-resilient, empowers rural clinics/cold-chains, though battery storage costs limit heavy industrial smelting [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the principles and stages of an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) under Zimbabwe's Environmental Management Agency (EMA) before approving a major open-cast mine or highway. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Purpose:** Precautionary decision tool weighing biophysical and socioeconomic impacts prior to project approval [4 marks].
- **Stages:** Screening → Scoping & Baseline Survey → Public Stakeholder Consultation → Impact Prediction & Mitigation Design (EMS) → EMA Review Decision → Post-implementation Auditing & Decommissioning bonds [11 marks].

questions.questionText: Assess the opportunities and challenges of Sustainable Ecotourism (including CAMPFIRE community conservation programmes) for rural livelihoods in Zimbabwe. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Mechanism:** Devolves wildlife benefits (photographic & safari revenues) to rural wards so communities value conservation over poaching [8 marks].
- **Evaluation:** Builds local clinics/schools and tolerates human-wildlife conflict when revenues reach households transparently; vulnerable to global travel shocks, governance leakage, and drought [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the Globalisation drivers (containerisation, TNCs, ICT) and evaluate why benefits of global trade have been distributed unevenly between core and developing economies. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Drivers:** Falling transport/communication costs, trade liberalisation, Transnational Corporations dispersing assembly globally [8 marks].
- **Uneven Distribution:** Value capture concentrates in R&D/brand hubs in core countries while developing nations face tariff escalation on processed exports, commodity price volatility, and infrastructure deficits [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Contrast Urban Renewal (Gentrification & Redevelopment) with Slum Upgrading ("Sites and Services") as strategies for improving low-income urban housing. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Demolition/Redevelopment:** Replaces dilapidated stock with modern apartments, but displaces poor residents to unserviced fringes and destroys social networks [9 marks].
- **In-situ Upgrading / Sites-and-Services:** Provides secure land tenure, piped water, sewerage, and incremental self-build plots—retains community cohesion and matches household budgets when paired with micro-mortgages [11 marks].

questions.questionText: Analyse the causes of Food Insecurity in semi-arid Regions IV and V of Zimbabwe and evaluate drought-resilient farming innovations (Pfumvudza/Intwasa, small grains, solar drip irrigation). [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Causes:** Erratic rainfall, dry spells, sandy nutrient-poor soils, post-harvest weevil losses, input price barriers [7 marks].
- **Remedies:** Conservation basins + mulching trap scarce moisture & organic fertility; drought-tolerant sorghum/millet/pearl millet outperform maize in dry years; small solar drip schemes boost winter nutrition [13 marks].

questions.questionText: Using Burgess/Bid-Rent curves, explain why commercial retail and finance concentrate at the Peak Land Value Intersection (CBD) and why "Out-of-Town" retail parks are expanding. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Bid-Rent:** Finance and flagship retail require maximum pedestrian accessibility and can outbid industry/housing per m² in the CBD core [8 marks].
- **Suburban Decentralisation:** Rising CBD congestion, parking scarcity, and high land rates push supermarkets and offices to accessible suburban hubs (e.g., Borrowdale/Msasa/Westgate) [7 marks].

questions.questionText: Distinguish between Renewable and Non-Renewable Energy transitions and evaluate the socio-economic barriers slowing adoption of clean cooking alternatives over fuelwood in rural areas. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Fuelwood Reliance:** ~60%+ rural energy uses wood/charcoal, driving deforestation around towns and indoor smoke respiratory illness [8 marks].
- **Barriers:** Upfront cost of LPG cylinders/stoves/biogas digesters, unreliable rural gas refilling networks, free collection of deadwood, cultural cooking preferences [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Evaluate the role of Transport Networks (Kansky's Beta & Gamma network connectivity indices, Beira/North-South corridors) in unlocking landlocked Zimbabwe's trade competitiveness. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Indices & Corridors:** Higher Beta (e/v) and Gamma indices measure network efficiency/redundancy; corridors linking Beitbridge, Forbes-Beira, and Chirundu connect inland mines/farms to sea ports [10 marks].
- **Evaluation:** Upgraded NRZ rail freight and one-stop border posts (Chirundu/Beitbridge) sharply lower bulk transit costs compared with overloaded haulage trucks damaging highways [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how Population Pyramids reflect Dependency Ratios and future planning needs for Education, Healthcare, and Pensions across contrasting countries. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Youthful Pyramid (Zimbabwe):** Wide base → high youth dependency ratio, urgent need for schools, maternal/paediatric health, and rapid formal job creation [8 marks].
- **Ageing Pyramid (Japan/UK):** Narrow base, broad apex → rising old-age dependency, pension funding strain, geriatric care, and labour automation needs [7 marks].

questions.questionText: Compare Spatial Allocation of Health Services and Water Supply between urban and rural districts, assessing the role of devolution in narrowing spatial inequality. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Disparities:** Urban centres concentrate referral hospitals, specialists, and piped supply; remote rural wards face long travel distances, seasonal boreholes, and referral delays [10 marks].
- **Devolution Assessment:** Directing fiscal grants to Rural District Councils targets local clinic and borehole priorities better if coupled with transparent audit capacity [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Evaluate how Agglomeration Economies and Industrial Inertia keep established manufacturing clusters (e.g., Workington/Msasa/Belmont) thriving even after original locational advantages change. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Internal & External Economies:** Shared skilled labour pool, component suppliers, utilities, repair services, and lower freight interchange costs [9 marks].
- **Inertia vs Diseconomies:** Sunk factory capital keeps firms anchored until traffic congestion, high municipal rates, and ageing infrastructure push decentralisation to outlying industrial parks [6 marks].

questions.questionText: Assess the socio-economic and environmental trade-offs of Rapid Peri-Urban Residential Sprawl on Harare's wetlands and agricultural greenbelt. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Pressures:** Housing backlog pushes unregulated subdivisions onto seasonal vlei wetlands and former market-gardening farms [7 marks].
- **Impacts & Policy:** Destroys natural flood sponges and Lake Chivero water filtration, increases cholera/borehole contamination risks, and lengthens commuter infrastructure costs; requires compact high-density infill and strict EMA wetland enforcement [13 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how a geographer uses Nearest Neighbour Analysis (Rₙ) to objectively classify rural settlement patterns (nucleated, random, or uniform/dispersed). [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Formula:** Rₙ = 2 · d̄_obs · √(n / A), where d̄_obs = mean distance to nearest neighbour, n = settlements, A = study area [6 marks].
- **Scale Interpretation:** Rₙ = 0 (completely clustered/nucleated—floodplain or borehole clusters); Rₙ = 1.0 (random); Rₙ ≈ 2.15 (uniform dispersed hexagonal spacing—regular smallholdings) [9 marks].
